transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I feel worn out all the time no matter how much I rest, like I don’t have any energy left to get through work or take care of things at home. It just feels like I'm completely running on empty every single day, and I don't know what to do anymore.

Along with feeling exhausted, have you been feeling down or hopeless, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy? Or does it feel more like stress and overwork without those mood changes?

It feels much more like constant, overwhelming stress, worry, and overwork rather than feeling down or hopeless. But because I'm so exhausted all the time, I've lost the sense of ease I used to find in gardening, fishing, and volunteering, and I end up skipping church events and time with my wife.

For at least the past two weeks, have you felt sad or hopeless most of the day nearly every day, or is it mainly exhaustion and stress without that kind of depressed mood? Also, even when you do have time and energy, are you still unable to enjoy things like gardening or being with your wife?

It’s definitely more about the constant exhaustion, worry, and stress rather than feeling deeply sad or hopeless. The constant worry has just eroded the sense of ease I used to get from gardening, and because I'm so drained and on edge by the time I get home, I find myself putting off spending quality time with my wife.

When you try to do something that takes concentration, like reading, paperwork, or making decisions, do you quickly feel mentally exhausted and unable to think clearly, or is it mainly a physical drained feeling from stress and overwork?

It’s honestly a mix of both. Mentally, my mind constantly drifts to worrying about bills, which makes me zone out and lose track of what I'm doing even when I'm ringing up customers at work. Physically, I feel exhausted from the moment I wake up, making basic things like standing at the register or cooking dinner feel incredibly draining.

Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different parts of life on most days, and is it hard to control the worrying even when you try? Or does the exhaustion feel mainly tied to being overworked and burned out rather than persistent uncontrollable worry?

Yes, the exhaustion is definitely tied to constant, uncontrollable worry rather than just normal burnout. My mind is always racing with worst-case scenarios about money, our car, or my mom, and once those thoughts start, they just snowball. I find it impossible to shut them off, even when I try to focus on other things.

When you try to rest or take time off, does the exhaustion improve at all, or do you still feel worn out and mentally drained even without much activity? Also, after small efforts like reading, conversations, or simple chores, do you quickly feel a marked increase in fatigue?

No, resting or taking days off doesn't help at all, and I still wake up feeling like I've already done a full day's work. Even simple things like cooking dinner for my family or standing at the register quickly drain the very last bit of energy I have.

When you’re worrying, do you also have symptoms like muscle tension, feeling keyed up or restless, irritability, trouble sleeping, or feeling on edge most days? Or is it mainly the exhaustion and mental fatigue without those anxiety symptoms?

It is definitely more than just exhaustion, as I struggle a lot with sleep, lying awake staring at the ceiling for hours with my mind racing, and then waking up early unable to settle back down. On top of that, I feel constantly tense and on edge, like I'm always waiting for something bad to happen.

Which feels more central to your problem: the nonstop worrying and feeling on edge, or the fatigue itself even when you are not especially worried? In other words, if the worrying eased, do you think the exhaustion would mostly improve too?

The constant worrying and tension definitely feel like the root cause of my exhaustion. All that mental racing and worst-case scenario thinking are what keep me awake at night and make me feel tense all day long. If I could finally quiet my mind and stop worrying, I really believe I would sleep better and wouldn't feel so completely drained.
How long have you been dealing with this excessive, hard-to-control worry and feeling on edge most days? Has it been going on for 6 months or longer?

Yes, it has been going on for much longer than six months, actually for about a year and three months now. It started right after my work hours were cut and my schedule became unpredictable, and it has been a continuous struggle that hasn't let up since.
